rules.why: Short entry after the price has already squeezed up since the signal and taker buying has faded. This catches the 'against_then_for' shape (MAE around 3h) after the adverse move is spent, so the entry is higher and the floor is further away.

Shorts on Bybit have been covering (the crowd shifted long) while price rose. This marks a short squeeze that has already happened; the forced buying is done, leaving a better price to short with less squeeze fuel left.

Open interest is unwinding during a rise after the signal. The rally is driven by liquidations or covering rather than new longs, so it tends to exhaust; entering after the unwind avoids the straight_against paths.

A burst of aggressive buying that ate through ask depth and lifted the price for an hour. This is a buying climax where exhaustion is likely, so shorting into it gives a better fill than entering at the signal.

Funding has turned positive and longs are paying while the price is at or above the signal price. Longs are getting crowded, and a short collects funding and gets in at a no-worse price than the signal.
Pump already happened (4h up >6%), buying burst has faded and OI is unwinding: late longs exiting, so shorting the exhausted top should lower adverse excursion versus entering at the signal hour.
Price ran against the signal (better short price), but taker flow has turned to selling and the crowd is not adding shorts. The squeeze risk is spent, so a 5% stop rarely hits the winners.
Positive funding means longs pay and are crowded. A 1h up-move on below-normal trade activity is a weak, thin rally, which makes a good fade entry for shorts.
Long-heavy crowd starts unwinding (OI falling, price turning down): a long liquidation cascade begins, so the short enters with momentum and little adverse excursion, which suits a tight 3% stop.
